html:
Kuuvuan KaNianiq is the land of the Inupiat of the Kobuk River in northwestern Alaska, the river that flows west into Kotzebue Sound. The Kobuk people were inland Inupiat who lived by hunting caribou, fishing for whitefish and salmon, and trading with the coast.

The valley is rich in history. At Onion Portage, a caribou crossing on the river, archaeologists found layers of camps spanning thousands of years. The nearby Jade Mountains gave jade for tools. Their neighbours upriver and to the south were the Athabaskan Koyukon. Today the villages of Ambler, Shungnak and Kobuk lie on the river.
